chapter: Kid Ory, Hampton, Ellington and Ben Webster
title: Ellington's speech captured in Beneath the Underdog
summary: Johnson marvels at Mingus's recall of Duke's mocking elegance in the book; Mingus calls it a spooky talent.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I asked you last time, but I didn't have to because it's in your book, that whole thing that sort of was the end of your stay with Ellington. But I want to ask you one more thing about that, because we goofed up last time.

I said, I knew pretty well, almost since I was a kid, and I have never seen anybody, including Mercer in his book on Duke or Stanley Dance, get the way Duke spoke, not only spoke, but the images and the whole mocking kind of humor, that elegance. This goes on for a couple of pages in your book, and it's as if you had a tape recorder there.
I have that talent, man, I don't know. I did it, like I told you, with a guy named Big Brown. It scared me, when I read it. It's like, a little spooky, ghostly.
It's like having perfect pitch for peoples' cadences and speech, I guess.
